title: Runtime slate adaptor hooks and timing probe - personal sketch
content:
Summary:

A freeform sketch for a small runtime "slate adaptor" layer and a lightweight timing probe used to evaluate prefill effectiveness and warmup latency across client-side and server-side caches.

Goal:
- Provide an extensible hook surface that can sit between ingress (client SDK or edge proxy) and the serving runtime to:
  - attach/validate slate metadata (compact prefill bundles),
  - orchestrate prefill warming (KV cache priming, local prefix caching),
  - emit fine-grained timing and outcome telemetry without blocking the main request fast path.

Why this?
- We see high variance in cold-start token latency when prefill bundles are either missing or partial.
- Need to measure the cost/benefit of prefill strategies (client prefill vs runtime prefill) in the wild with minimal signal noise.
- Want to be able to A/B different prefill heuristics and tie them to cost metrics per-route.

High-level design (text diagram):

[Client/Edge] -> [Ingress Router] -> [Slate Adaptor Hooks & Probe] -> [Serving Runtime] -> [Model]
                         |                          ^
                         v                          |
                    (async warmers) -----------------

Key components:
1) Slate Adaptor Hooks (sync):
   - validate_slate(slate_meta): quick rules (size, TTL, signature)
   - classify_prefill_intent(slate_meta): {required, suggested, hint-only}
   - rewrite_context_for_runtime(context, slate_meta): attach minimal control headers

   Requirements:
   - Must be <500us median on hot path for 99th-percentile latency-sensitive routes.
   - No heavyweight crypto on hot path; signature verification can be deferred to async path for non-critical cases.

2) Timing Probe (sync + async telemetry):
   - Emit event markers: ingress_receive, slate_validation_done, prefill_triggered, runtime_prefill_hit, runtime_prefill_miss, model_stream_start, model_stream_end.
   - Probe should support sampling (per-route and reservoir sampling) and must attach lightweight correlation ids to trace.

3) Async Warmers (fire-and-forget):
   - If slate classified as "suggested" and runtime cache missing, enqueue a warmer to prime KV / prefix cache.
   - Warmers run in separate worker pool with backpressure and cost budget.
   - Warmers must report "warmer_result" events for later attribution.

API shape sketches (example wire formats as plain text):

- Slate metadata header (compact, base64-like payload):
  X-Redwood-Slate: v1:sz=1024;ttl=3600;hint=topic:refund;sig=ABCD1234

- Lightweight slate manifest (payload for async warmers):
  {"slate_id":"s_123","items":[{"type":"prefix","hash":"h1","len":128},{"type":"kv","key":"k_user_42"}],"scoring":{"priority":5}}
  (this JSON is stored in async queue only; not sent inline on hot path)

- Timing probe beacon (sync header for correlation):
  X-Redwood-Probe: id=trace-xxxxx;sample=1

Operational knobs (config sketch):
- per_route: { sampling_rate, async_warmer_budget_tokens_per_min, max_prefill_items, prefer_client_prefill }
- global: { max_concurrent_warmers, cold_hit_threshold_ms, validation_timeout_ms }

Example config snippet (informal):
- route:/chat/complete -> sampling_rate=0.02, async_warmer_budget_tokens_per_min=5000, prefer_client_prefill=true
- route:/assistant/summary -> sampling_rate=0.1, async_warmer_budget_tokens_per_min=20000, prefer_client_prefill=false

Telemetry / metrics to record (important for experiments):
- prefill_attempts_total (by route, type:client/runtime/async)
- prefill_hits_runtime (by slab key/prefix)
- prefill_warmer_runs_success/failed
- warmup_latency_ms (distribution)
- added_tokens_served_due_to_prefill (estimate)
- per-request extra_latency_ms_due_to_validation (p50/p95/p99)

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- signature verification: do we move all signature checks to async and accept a small risk on hot path? Where are customers that require strict attestation?
- eviction semantics: if warmers prime lots of items we might thrash runtime KV; need a tenant quota and ttl-slope policy.
- cost attribution: how to attribute warmer cost if warmed but never used? Propose a 24h attribution window and probabilistic amortization.
- client vs runtime prefill: sometimes client prefill is stale; we need heuristics to compare freshness and favour runtime if stale > X seconds.
- provenance: include a provenance header that indicates who initiated prefill (client/user/automated-warner) to aid forensics.

Mini experiment plan (quick A/B):
- A: no runtime warmers, client only prefill (sampling 1%).
- B: enable runtime warmers for suggested slates, sampler 1%, warmers budget 1000 tokens/min.
- Metric: model_stream_start latency p95 and 24h extra tokens billed. Secondary: prefill_warmer_runs_success rate.

Implementation notes / TODOs:
- Build adaptor hooks as a small module inside ingress router (so it can be toggled per-tenant).
- Add lightweight probe integration to existing tracing library (open-telemetry).
- Wire an async queue (existing runtime-warmers) and extend worker to accept slate manifests.
- Add per-route config to Console (feature flag initial rollout).

References (internal):
- Linear: DEV-2145 (measurement harness for prefill warmers)
- GH: runtime PR #812 (initial warmers worker)
- Slack thread: #runtime-prefill (thread: "prefill budget vs latency")

Quick sketches / mental model (one-liners):
- "Slate": compact hint bundle about context segments worth preloading.
- "Adaptor hooks": safety belt that keeps validation cheap and delegates heavy lifting off the hot path.
- "Warmers": asynchronous priming agents that must be budgeted and sampled.

Notes to self: keep the hot path tiny. This is a measurement-first feature; iterate quickly with sampling on a few low-risk routes before wide rollout.

Unresolved: who owns per-tenant warmer budget in Console? product or infra? Ask @Marta in next sync.

-- end of sketch --
